system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller issued a service ticket for svc-bkp to FILE-HD-01$ with the request attributed to public IP 45.79.19.196. The supplied environment context says there is no VPN and identifies svc-bkp as a backup agent account on FILE-HD-01, making this external-source authentication anomalous and consistent with unauthorized credential use.

About three seconds after that ticket event, FILE-HD-01 recorded a service logon for svc-bkp. This establishes nearby use of the account, but does not by itself prove the logon was caused by the external request.

FILE-HD-01 subsequently launched the approved CobaltVault agent as svc-bkp, targeting ingest.cobaltvault.net; proxy records show access to that approved destination. This is a plausible benign explanation for an outbound backup transfer, but the records do not establish that it accounts for the alert's reported volume or timing.

FILE-HD-01 made an SMB connection to DC-HD-01 that was associated with an ANONYMOUS LOGON NTLM network logon. This is an additional unusual event in the review window, although the records do not show what SMB resource or operation was involved.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not show an outbound connection from FILE-HD-01 to the public Internet carrying hundreds of megabytes around 13:46 UTC. The CobaltVault-related proxy records are around 13:50 UTC and report only small tunnel byte counts, so they do not independently verify the alert's reported transfer volume (T030-00285, T030-00287, T030-00292).
The records do not identify the files, contents, or destination-side receipt for any large transfer.
The external-IP ticket event and the later local svc-bkp service logon are close in time, but the available records do not establish a causal link between them (T030-00269, T030-00270).
claims_not_established: That the reported hundreds-of-megabytes transfer was to CobaltVault, or that it was the result of the observed CobaltVault agent run.
That the public-IP svc-bkp ticket request directly initiated the local svc-bkp service logon or the backup-agent execution.
What data, if any, was transferred externally, or whether any data was exfiltrated.
Who controlled public IP 45.79.19.196 or whether the authentication reflects compromised credentials, a misconfiguration, or another cause.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the network-monitoring alert details and flow records, including exact start/end time, destination IP/domain, transferred byte counts, and protocol, to verify the reported transfer.
Review DC-HD-01 authentication and Kerberos logs around T030-00269 for the requesting client, related logons, and other use of svc-bkp; validate whether 45.79.19.196 is an authorized source.
Collect FILE-HD-01 CobaltVault agent logs, job results, and file-selection/transfer records for the run around 13:50 UTC, and compare them with the alert's volume and timing.
Investigate the SMB session at T030-00242 using SMB share/file-access auditing and related host telemetry to determine its purpose.
Preserve and review FILE-HD-01 service, account, and endpoint-security telemetry for evidence of unauthorized changes or follow-on activity.
